conviction_note: The evidence is close to balanced. A likely revenue beat against a consensus that sits below Q2's own revenue, plus a fresh short build, is offset by the founder's 10b5-1 selling right up to the print, a GAAP charge of about $35M, and no sign yet of the Edge launch that management slated for the fall. The swing factor is the first 2027 outlook for the combined company with Freddie, which the company itself scheduled for this call and whose direction I cannot source. So p_up is 51 on a 12-point absolute move, which gives +0.24, and the per-finding sum is +0.2. The two measurements agree.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $136.4M (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/GRND/22297, 2026-10-28) and $136.6M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GRND/earnings-forecasts); two sources agree. EPS consensus is $0.16 (Earnings Whispers, Kalshi), or $0.15 (Benzinga). The company guide is FY2026 revenue about $540M and adj. EBITDA about $232M (Q2 letter, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000023/shl_q2x2026xfinal.htm). H1 was $268.1M, which leaves about $271.9M for H2. There is no consensus for the 2027 outlook. Aggregators put 2027 revenue at $592M-$617M, with unclear dates and most likely without Freddie, so the guidance bar is effectively unsourced.
positioning_check: Short interest was 8.32M shares as of 2026-10-15 with 4.0 days to cover (massive.com/quote/grnd, read 2026-11-05). That is up from 5.64M and 3.5 days at 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis/curvedtrading via search). Against shares outstanding of 173.8M it is about 4.8%. Against shares not held by Zage's group (about 80M), it is about 10%. That is building but not crowded. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +4.0 vol points, a mild downside paid. Put/call open interest is 0.19, so call-heavy. The ATM spread is 40% of mid, so the 13.69% event-implied move is only indicative. The stock is down about 18% since the Q2 print and sits near its post-earnings low (Earnings Whispers, 2026-10-28). It is +5.4% over 5 days.

findings.finding: The company itself scheduled an initial 2027 outlook for the combined Grindr + Freddie (PurposeMed) for this Q3 call, so this print carries a first guide for a new year. Freddie's 2026 revenue is expected above $80M with adj. EBITDA above $10M (about 12.5% margin), against Grindr's FY26 guide of about $540M revenue and about $232M adj. EBITDA at roughly 43%. So the combined 2027 headline revenue should land well above the $592M-$617M aggregator 2027 figures, which most likely exclude Freddie. The combined margin will be diluted below the 39-42% long-term target the company reaffirmed. The core-growth guide is the unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 raised the FY guide by $5M on a 4.3% revenue beat and the stock fell 3.3% (baseline). In Q3 2025 the revenue guide was reaffirmed, EBITDA guidance was raised, and the stock rose 11.0%. In Q1 2026 the guide was raised to $535M and the stock rose 9.3% (baseline). Guidance direction has decided the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: No published 2027 consensus includes Freddie; the aggregator 2027 figures ($592M-$617M) predate or ignore it. If the market had priced a margin-dilutive combined guide, previews would quote a combined 2027 number. Instead the Oct 28 preview frames 2027 only as Edge versus a growth fade and does not mention Freddie.
findings.independence: The press release in the same 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000033/exhibit991-pressreleasedat.htm) says the same, so it is one document family. The Nov 2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000036/grnd-20261102.htm) confirms the deal closed on Nov 2, so Freddie consolidates from Q4. The sign is my inference: a company that chooses to give an early outlook is usually comfortable with it.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue consensus is $136.4M-$136.6M, below Q2 2026's reported $138.1M. That is a sequential decline and only +17.8% year on year against Q3 2025's $115.8M. Q2 showed average paying users of 1.4M (+16% YoY) and ARPPU of $26.51 (+12%), and management wrote it is 'performing ahead of what we expected coming into the year'. The last three revenue prints beat: Q2 2026 by 4.3% ($138.1M vs $132.4M), Q3 2025 by 2.2% ($115.8M vs $113.3M). A Q3 at merely flat sequential revenue ($138M) would beat by about 1.2%. A Q3 2025-style sequential gain would beat by 3-5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have bought mixed reactions. Q3 2025's 2.2% beat bought +11.0%; Q2 2026's 4.3% beat was sold (-3.3% in the baseline, -6.7% after hours per one recap). This name does not reliably pay for a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus below the prior quarter's revenue means the Street has taken management's flat-H2 guide literally. If the market expected a beat, previews would carry a whisper above $138M, and the stock would not sit 18% below the last print near its post-earnings low.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/GRND/22297, 2026-10-28) for the bar. Q3 2025 beat history: https://www.itiger.com/news/2581046171. The Q2 beat size comes from aggregator search results. Management guided to H2 deceleration as 2025 price increases lap, which caps the size.

findings.finding: Grindr agreed on 2026-09-02 to settle the UK privacy group action for GBP 26M (about $35M): GBP 13M due by 2026-12-31 and GBP 13M by 2027-03-31. The Q2 10-Q showed only $2.6M of accrued legal contingencies at June 30, so most of the charge should hit Q3 GAAP results, about $0.15-0.20 a share before any tax effect, against a $0.16 EPS consensus. Grindr adds back litigation costs in adj. EBITDA, so the guided EBITDA line is unaffected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GAAP EPS was reported as a miss ($0.10 vs $0.15-0.16 per aggregators) alongside a revenue beat, and the stock fell 3.3%. That GAAP-line reaction cannot be separated from the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether the $0.16 consensus includes the charge is not visible. If it did, previews would show Q3 EPS well below the year-ago $0.16 rather than 'flat with the year-ago quarter'. The charge has no path to the guide, so it is sized as a headline-only item.
findings.independence: The Hacker News, 2026-09-08 (https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/grindr-to-pay-26-million-to-settle-uk.html), gives the $35.1M figure. The accrual of $2.6M at June 30 comes from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000025/grnd-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Grindr had $6.5M of cash at 2026-06-30, a $390M term loan, and an undrawn $200M revolver. It paid $190M in cash for PurposeMed at the Nov 2 close and owes GBP 26M of settlement payments by March 2027. So net debt rises to roughly $560M+, about 2.4x the FY26 adj. EBITDA guide, and buybacks are already 'more opportunistic'. The money buys a business with revenue above $80M that adds EBITDA dollars, so the sign is near zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on leverage. The stock fell 4.3% on the day of the deal announcement, before it was public, and moved little after (Stocktwits).
findings.why_not_priced: The deal terms are public, and the funding route (a revolver draw or new debt) and the hit to buyback capacity will first be shown in the Q3 letter and balance sheet. If the market had priced it, the stock would have reacted to the deal more than it did.
findings.independence: The Nov 2 8-K confirms the $190M of cash paid at close (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000036/grnd-20261102.htm). The Q2 letter says buybacks are more opportunistic and about $300M remains authorized.

findings.finding: Director and 53.8% holder Ray Zage sold 2,000,000 shares from 2026-09-16 to 2026-11-03 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-06-17, at falling prices from $15.62 down to $12.78. That includes 330,000 shares on Nov 2 and 170,000 on Nov 3, the two sessions before the print. The 13D/A of 2026-11-04 gives no plan size or end date, so supply may continue through the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print overlapped a Zage sale programme. The 2025 take-private bid by the same holder was withdrawn, and the stock fell on it.
findings.why_not_priced: The 13D/A was filed one day before the print and shows the controlling holder selling into weakness. That is a steady seller of about 4-15% of daily volume on its selling days. A market that had priced it would not show call-heavy open interest (put/call 0.19).
findings.independence: Form 4 of 2026-11-04 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000183367826000009/xslF345X06/form4-11042026_041102.xml); same holder, same sales. Other officer filings in October (Arison, North) were tax withholding (code F); Katz sold 15,227 shares under a plan.

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 8.32M shares, 4.0 days to cover, at the 2026-10-15 settlement, from 5.64M (3.5 days) at 2026-09-30. That is about 10% of the shares outside Zage's group, built into a stock already near its post-earnings low. It gives a moderate covering mechanism if the 2027 outlook is acceptable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observable from the baseline. Two of the eight prior reactions exceeded +9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Shorts added about 2.7M shares in two weeks, into the print. This is a positioning fact, not information about the quarter. Had it been unwound, the next settlement would show it. Aggregators disagree on levels (equibles showed 8.7M at 2026-08-19).
findings.independence: Search result attributing 5.64M shares and 3.5 days at 2026-09-30 to stockanalysis/curvedtrading (FINRA data). Lower-quality aggregator sources.

findings.finding: Edge, the AI premium tier ($80-$200 a week in testing) that management calls a primary 2027 growth driver, was 'slated for a fall launch' per the 2026-10-28 preview. I found no global launch announcement through 2026-11-05. The Q2 letter gave no date and said Q2 was spent 'refining the branding, packaging, and positioning'. A launch slipping into 2027 would weaken the Q4 exit rate and the core 2027 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 positioned Edge as the 2027 driver alongside a modest raise, and the stock fell 3.3%. There is no earlier Edge-specific reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews still frame Edge as a fall launch. If a slip were priced, previews would treat 2027 as a fade, not a 'managed handoff'. This finding rests partly on an absence (no launch announcement), so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 shareholder letter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820144/000182014426000023/shl_q2x2026xfinal.htm). The TechCrunch report via secondary sources says broader launch is 'toward the end of 2026 or in early 2027'. Shares the 2027-outlook event with finding 1 but rests on a different fact.

findings.finding: Peer Match Group reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-02, after Grindr last spoke. Tinder daily active users returned to year-over-year growth in September for the first time in about 3.5 years, and Hinge posted double-digit growth in users, revenue and payers. That is a modestly positive read-across for online dating demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline history on peer read-across.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: GRND is +5.4% over 5 days since Match's release. Grindr's niche user base is a weak proxy for Tinder/Hinge, so this is filed as a proxy.

outside_window.finding: Freddie earnout of up to $70M in cash, tied to 2027 targets and payable in 2028; the second GBP 13M settlement payment is due by 2027-03-31.

Revived take-private proposal from Zage or Lu in 2026: none; the 13D/A of 2026-11-04 states no proposal
Edge global launch announcement, Sept-Nov 2026: none found

Explanation for the mid-to-late October drop from about $15.2 to $12.8: no news cause found besides Zage's 10b5-1 sales and the deal
Analyst previews with a 2027 number that includes Freddie: none found

baseline_tension: The mild put skew (+4) and the 18% slide since the last print agree with the negatives (Zage supply, the GAAP charge, the Edge timing). The call-heavy open interest, a fresh short build and a below-Q2 revenue bar cut the other way. Net, nothing beats the skew decisively, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the revenue-beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6, because Q2's 4.3% beat was sold.
Rule 2 (one-offs as one-offs): the UK settlement charge cut from -0.5 to -0.3; it is below adj. EBITDA and has no path to the guide.
Rule 3 (your own caveat reaches the number): the 2027 outlook finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because its sign is my inference.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the leverage finding re-signed toward zero, -0.3 to -0.1; the cash buys a business with over $80M of revenue that adds EBITDA dollars.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest looked up (8.32M, 4.0 days to cover, not crowded); Zage selling trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4; the short-build finding left at +0.3.
Rule 5 (proxy and absence): Edge no-launch finding cut from -0.5 to -0.3 as partly an absence; Match read-across cut from +0.2 to +0.1 as a proxy already in the 5-day run-up.
The sum is unchanged at +0.2, and abs_move_pct and p_up are unchanged.
